paper_title: Center-vortex semiclassics with non-minimal 't Hooft fluxes on $\mathbb R^2\times T^2$ and center stabilization at large $N$ (Hayashi, 2026, JHEP)
core_reasoning_8:
\textbf{Claim.}
For a Wilson loop $W_R(C)$ of $N$-ality $|R|$ and area $A:=\operatorname{Area}(C)$, the dilute center-vortex gas gives the infinite-volume area law
\[
\langle W_R(C)\rangle=\exp[-T_R(\theta)A]
\]
with
\[
T_R(\theta)=2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}
\left[
\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{N}\right)-
\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi q|R|}{N}\right)
\right].
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &pq\equiv1\pmod N,
\quad |R|\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z,
\quad A:=\operatorname{Area}(C).\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\text{A vortex inside }C\text{ shifts }\theta\mapsto\theta+2\pi q|R|\text{ in its Boltzmann phase.}\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &E_k(\theta)=-2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}\cos\left(\frac{\theta-2\pi k}{N}\right).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\langle W_R(C)\rangle=
Z_{\mathrm{eff},\theta}^{-1}
\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}e^{-VE_k(\theta)}
\exp[-A(E_k(\theta+2\pi q|R|)-E_k(\theta))].\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{For }-\pi<\theta<\pi\text{ and }V\to\infty,\text{ the }k=0\text{ branch dominates.}\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &1-\cos(2x)=2\sin^2x.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
\langle W_R(C)\rangle
&=\exp[-A(E_0(\theta+2\pi q|R|)-E_0(\theta))]
&&\text{by (P4) and (P5)}\\
&=:\exp[-T_R(\theta)A]
&&\text{definition of }T_R(\theta).
\end{align}
\begin{align}
T_R(\theta)
&=E_0(\theta+2\pi q|R|)-E_0(\theta)
&&\text{from the preceding line}\\
&=-2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi q|R|}{N}\right)
+2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}
\left[
\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{N}\right)-
\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi q|R|}{N}\right)
\right]
&&\text{algebra}.
\end{align}
At $\theta=0$,
\begin{align}
T_R(0)
&=2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}\left[1-\cos\left(\frac{2\pi q|R|}{N}\right)\right]
&&\text{set }\theta=0\\
&=4K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi q|R|}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P6)}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
\langle W_R(C)\rangle=e^{-T_R(\theta)A},
\qquad
T_R(\theta)=2K e^{-8\pi^2/(Ng^2)}
\left[
\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{N}\right)-
\cos\left(\frac{\theta+2\pi q|R|}{N}\right)
\right]
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_11:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the large-$N$ string-tension formula
\[
T_r=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi q r}{N}\right),
\qquad r:=|R|,
\]
with $pq\equiv1\pmod N$, every representation with $r=kp$ and fixed $k=O(1)$ has
\[
T_{kp}=O(N^{-2}).
\]
Therefore large-$N$ one-form center stability requires all light charges $r=O(1)$ to have $qr=O(N)$ modulo $N$.

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &pq\equiv1\pmod N.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &T_r:=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi q r}{N}\right),\quad \sigma>0.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &r=kp,
\quad k=O(1)\text{ as }N\to\infty.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &pq=1+Ns\text{ for some }s\in\mathbb Z.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\sin^2(x+\pi m)=\sin^2x\text{ for }m\in\mathbb Z.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\sin x=x+O(x^3)\text{ as }x\to0.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\text{A light charge is confined at large }N\text{ only if its limiting tension is nonzero.}
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
T_{kp}
&=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi qkp}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P2) and (P3)}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi k(1+Ns)}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi k}{N}+\pi ks\right)
&&\text{algebra}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi k}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\sigma\left(\frac{\pi k}{N}+O(N^{-3})\right)^2
&&\text{by (P6), since }k=O(1)\\
&=O(N^{-2})
&&\text{collect powers of }N.
\end{align}
For a light charge $r=O(1)$,
\begin{align}
T_r\to0
&\Longleftarrow \frac{qr}{N}\to0\pmod1
&&\text{by (P2) and continuity of }\sin^2\\
&\Longleftrightarrow qr=O(1)\pmod N.
\end{align}
Therefore, to avoid vanishing tension for every nonzero light charge,
\begin{align}
qr&=O(N)\pmod N
&&\text{by (P7)}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
T_{kp}=O(N^{-2})\quad(k=O(1)),
\qquad
\text{large-}N\text{ stability requires }qr=O(N)\pmod N\text{ for all fixed }r\neq0
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_13:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the Fibonacci choice
\[
N=F_{n+2},
\qquad
p=F_n,
\]
where $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$, and $F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n$, the integer $q=(-1)^nF_n$ satisfies $pq\equiv1\pmod N$. For every fixed nonzero $N$-ality $r$, the large-$n$ string tension tends to
\[
\sigma\sin^2(\pi\phi r)>0,
\qquad
\phi:=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &F_0=0,
\quad F_1=1,
\quad F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &N:=F_{n+2},
\quad p:=F_n,
\quad q:=(-1)^nF_n.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &F_{n+1}^2-F_nF_{n+2}=(-1)^n.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &F_{n+1}=F_{n+2}-F_n.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &T_r:=\sigma\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi q r}{N}\right),
\quad r\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\},
\quad \sigma>0.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &F_n=\frac{\phi^n-(-\phi)^{-n}}{\sqrt5},
\quad \phi:=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},
\quad \phi^2=\phi+1.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\sin^2(-x)=\sin^2x,
\quad \sin^2(x+2\pi m)=\sin^2x\text{ for }m\in\mathbb Z.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\phi\notin\mathbb Q.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
First derive the modular inverse.
\begin{align}
F_{n+1}^2-F_nF_{n+2}
&=(-1)^n
&&\text{by (P3)}\\
(F_{n+2}-F_n)^2-F_nF_{n+2}
&=(-1)^n
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
F_{n+2}^2-3F_nF_{n+2}+F_n^2
&=(-1)^n
&&\text{expand and collect terms}\\
F_n^2
&\equiv (-1)^n\pmod{F_{n+2}}
&&\text{reduce modulo }F_{n+2}.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
pq
&=F_n((-1)^nF_n)
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=(-1)^nF_n^2
&&\text{algebra}\\
&\equiv1\pmod{F_{n+2}}
&&\text{by }F_n^2\equiv(-1)^n\pmod{F_{n+2}}\\
&\equiv1\pmod N
&&\text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}
Next compute the limiting ratio:
\begin{align}
\frac{|q|}{N}
&=\frac{F_n}{F_{n+2}}
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=\frac{\phi^n-(-\phi)^{-n}}{\phi^{n+2}-(-\phi)^{-(n+2)}}
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&\longrightarrow\frac{1}{\phi^2}
&&\text{divide by }\phi^n\text{ and take }n\to\infty\\
&=\frac{1}{1+\phi}
&&\text{by }\phi^2=\phi+1\\
&=2-\phi
&&\text{because }(2-
\phi)(1+
\phi)=1.
\end{align}
For fixed $r\neq0$,
\begin{align}
\lim_{n\to\infty}T_r
&=\sigma\sin^2\left(\pi r\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{|q|}{N}\right)
&&\text{by (P5) and (P7)}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2(\pi r(2-
\phi))
&&\text{substitute the ratio limit}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2(2\pi r-
\pi\phi r)
&&\text{algebra}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2(\pi\phi r)
&&\text{by (P7)}.
\end{align}
Finally,
\begin{align}
\sigma\sin^2(\pi\phi r)=0
&\Longrightarrow \phi r=m\text{ for some }m\in\mathbb Z
&&\text{zeros of }\sin\\
&\Longrightarrow \phi=m/r\in\mathbb Q
&&\text{because }r\neq0\\
&\Longrightarrow \text{contradiction with (P8)}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
pq\equiv1\pmod N,
\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty}T_r=\sigma\sin^2(\pi\phi r)>0
\quad(r\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_14:
\textbf{Claim.}
If $|q|/N\to\xi$ and a continued-fraction convergent $c_k/d_k$ of $\xi$ obeys
\[
\left|\xi-\frac{c_k}{d_k}\right|<\frac{1}{a_{k+1}d_k^2},
\]
then the string tension of the charge $r=d_k$ is bounded asymptotically by
\[
T_{d_k}\lesssim \sigma\left(\frac{\pi}{a_{k+1}d_k}\right)^2.
\]
Thus a very large coefficient $a_{k+1}$ creates an accidentally small tension.

\textbf{Premises.}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad &T_r:=\sigma\sin^2(\pi\xi r),
\quad \sigma>0,
\quad r=d_k.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\left|\xi-\frac{c_k}{d_k}\right|<\frac{1}{a_{k+1}d_k^2},
\quad a_{k+1}\in\mathbb Z_{>0},
\quad c_k,d_k\in\mathbb Z,
\quad d_k>0.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\sin^2(x+\pi m)=\sin^2x\text{ for }m\in\mathbb Z.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &|\sin x|\le |x|\text{ for all real }x.
\end{align*}

\textbf{Derivation.}
From (P2), there exists a real $\varepsilon_k$ such that
\begin{align}
\xi
&=\frac{c_k}{d_k}+\varepsilon_k
&&\text{definition of the approximation error}\\
|\varepsilon_k|
&<\frac{1}{a_{k+1}d_k^2}
&&\text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}
For $r=d_k$,
\begin{align}
T_{d_k}
&=\sigma\sin^2(\pi\xi d_k)
&&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=\sigma\sin^2(\pi(c_k+\varepsilon_k d_k))
&&\text{substitute }\xi=c_k/d_k+\varepsilon_k\\
&=\sigma\sin^2(\pi\varepsilon_k d_k)
&&\text{by (P3), since }c_k\in\mathbb Z\\
&\le \sigma(\pi\varepsilon_k d_k)^2
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&<\sigma\left(\frac{\pi}{a_{k+1}d_k}\right)^2
&&\text{use }|\varepsilon_k|<1/(a_{k+1}d_k^2).
\end{align}
If $a_{k+1}\gg1$, the final upper bound is parametrically smaller by $a_{k+1}^{-2}$.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{
T_{d_k}\lesssim \sigma\left(\frac{\pi}{a_{k+1}d_k}\right)^2,
\qquad
a_{k+1}\gg1\Longrightarrow T_{d_k}\text{ is accidentally suppressed}
}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
